blocks.goal: Extract the predefined/default Safelist factory methods (static constructors that create common configurations) into a new cohesive helper class so the Safelist class has fewer public methods and reduced responsibility (construction/presets separated from safelist behavior).

expected_impact.rationale: The five public static factory methods none(), simpleText(), basic(), basicWithImages(), and relaxed() (which together constitute a cohesive "preset/constructor" responsibility) are moved to a new Safelists helper class. This reduces the public API surface of Safelist by 5 public methods and moves a substantial chunk of LOC related to presets into a separate class, improving modularization.

ops.details: Create a new class org.jsoup.safety.Safelists that contains the five static factory/preset methods previously defined in Safelist: none(), simpleText(), basic(), basicWithImages(), and relaxed(). Remove these methods from Safelist. The new class resides in the same package and returns Safelist instances by calling the Safelist ctor and instance configuration methods (addTags, addAttributes, addProtocols, addEnforcedAttribute). No behavior change: callers that use these presets will need to reference Safelists.<preset>() instead of Safelist.<preset>().
Move the none() static factory method implementation to Safelists.none(). Remove the method from Safelist.
Move the simpleText() static factory method implementation to Safelists.simpleText(). Remove the method from Safelist.
Move the basic() static factory method implementation to Safelists.basic(). Remove the method from Safelist.
Move the basicWithImages() static factory method implementation to Safelists.basicWithImages(). Remove the method from Safelist.
Move the relaxed() static factory method implementation to Safelists.relaxed(). Remove the method from Safelist.

Update related tests affected by this refactoring block so the configured build command passes. Adjust imports, package references, moved class references, constructors, and assertions only when required. Do not change production behavior through tests.
